prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant. Aliases: Ironwood=River Intake Pump Station; Marigold=Coagulant Dosing Skid; Cobalt=North Filter Gallery; Sparrow=Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench; Lantern=SCADA Historian Server; Quarry=Maintenance Planner; Juniper=High Service Pump Header; Falcon=Distribution Dispatcher. Items: Raw Water Screen Channel→Quarry:Rake Torque Snapshot; Marigold→Laboratory Technician:Alum Batch Ticket; technician produces Sample Chain Slip; Sparrow receives samples/produces checked Jar Test Photograph Set(“the set”=dose confirmation); South Filter Gallery→Chief Operator:Filter Run Exception Note; Chemical Supplier Driver:Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log pre-unloading; Clearwell Level Controller:Clearwell Diver Entry Permit after level/isolation checks; Juniper:threshold-triggered Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; Chief Operator:verified Backwash Solids Manifest; Residuals Hauler removes residuals; Falcon sends verified Pressure Zone Handoff Card. Operations: intake permissives/alarm-stop; Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode. Approved dosing; unreliable indications hold approved dose. Sample custody/acceptance; late/warm troubleshooting-only. Backwash Recovery Tank return needs settling/clarity. Cobalt staggers verified washes; South breakthrough/delayed-ripening exclusion pending approval. Maintenance/overrides require approval/isolation/monitoring/evidence/restoration. Upsets escalate to Duty Engineer; Chlorine Residual Alarm pauses maintenance/capacity increases. Chlorine Contact Basin/clearwell monitor contact/storage/demand. Juniper compares pressure/reservoir/pump/field trends; informs Falcon of North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station reserve impacts. Automatic approved sequencing; manual/local recorded; communications-loss retains confirmed mode. Radio/phone coordination specifies stations/valves/pressure direction/completion. Normal restoration requires stable zones, cleared/assigned alarms, accounted fieldwork, unrestricted Chief Operator. Security: named role-based accounts; no routine shared credentials at listed process elements. Operators area-limited; engineering changes separately approved. Remote access:MFA/encryption/business-reason/Chief Operator-or-Duty Engineer approval. Quarry weekly maintenance-access review/reassignment revocation. Lantern critical; networks segmented/documented pathways; patches/firmware/antivirus tested predeployment. Alarms: Chief Operator governance; Duty Engineer limit-review support. Prioritize consequence/response-time/action/capability-loss; compliance/public-health Chlorine Residual Alarm high-priority.

New part:
S213: During Storm Intake Mode, alarm response expectations shall account for higher debris load, faster raw water quality changes, and increased dependence on intake screening and chemical dose verification.
S214: Backup power shall support safe operation or controlled shutdown of the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, SCADA Historian Server, High Service Pump Header, and essential control-room equipment.
S215: The plant shall maintain written expectations for generator start time, automatic transfer performance, fuel availability, and operator checks during extended utility outages.
S216: Uninterruptible power supplies shall be sized to bridge transfer events and allow orderly shutdown of servers, network switches, control processors, and communication equipment.
S217: Loss of both normal and standby power to a critical service shall be treated as an emergency operating condition requiring immediate notification of the Chief Operator and Duty Engineer.
S218: The Chief Operator has authority to direct emergency operating priorities when treatment, storage, distribution pressure, or personnel safety is at risk.
S219: The Duty Engineer may authorize temporary control workarounds during an emergency, but the workaround shall be logged, bounded by time or condition, and removed when normal control is restored.
S220: The Distribution Dispatcher shall be informed when failures at the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station may affect pressure zones or fire-flow readiness.
S221: The Laboratory Technician shall retain access needed for sample status review and reporting, but laboratory accounts shall not allow control actions on plant equipment.
S222: The Maintenance Planner uses the permit to verify isolation boundaries before confined-space work is released.
S223: The Duty Engineer reviews the Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before accepting a change in chlorine storage status.
S224: Reliability targets for critical plant services shall include prompt detection of failed sensors, redundant communication paths where practical, recoverable configuration backups, and periodic restoration testing.
S225: After any cybersecurity event, major alarm failure, or emergency control action, the Chief Operator shall require a brief operational review that identifies the cause, affected services, corrective actions, and any needed procedure changes.
S226: Commissioning shall be planned as a controlled sequence that proves each control function before the plant relies on it for normal service.
S227: Each commissioning test shall have defined starting conditions, expected responses, acceptance limits, and a responsible reviewer.
S228: Before wet commissioning begins, the Duty Engineer shall confirm that temporary controls, bypasses, and manual operating instructions are understood by the affected staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
